variant_decisions.evidence: Qere יָצִיעַ and ketiv יצוע are the same noun (lemma 3326 b), tagged Ncmsa in both; the ketiv writes the waw where the qere writes yod, so the difference is orthographic and the sense "story, side-structure" is unchanged. ASV "he built stories round about" renders either spelling, and the only note in the verse, "That is, the most holy place", maps to "the oracle" rather than to this word. Nothing in the English distinguishes the readings, so the decision is underdetermined and the qere base is retained.

variant_decisions.evidence: Here the readings differ morphologically, not just orthographically: qere מִשְׁפָּטָיו is plural (Ncmpc/Sp3ms) and ketiv משפטו singular (Ncmsc/Sp3ms), the same lemma 4941 with the same 3ms suffix. ASV reads "and according to all the fashion of it", but "fashion" is a mass noun in this sense, so "all the fashion of it" shows no number and would stand for either reading; contrast the preceding plural דבריו, which the countable "all the parts thereof" does show. The verse's note, "Or, with all the appurtenances thereof, and with all the ordinances thereof", is an alternative rendering of the sense of the two nouns rather than a textual note, and its plural "ordinances" simply parallels "appurtenances", so it does not attest a reading against the main text's "fashion". With the main text non-committal and the note not text-critical, the decision is underdetermined and the qere base is retained.
